title: Verdant Labs - On-prem / Air-gapped Deployment Discovery
next_steps: Redwood to share on-prem install guide and air-gap checklist
Verdant to provide hardware inventory + network diagram
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting week of 2026-03-09
SE to run compatibility pre-check with provided CUDA/driver versions
action_items: Alan Zhou | Share GPU inventory (model, memory, NVLink / InfiniBand topology) | 2026-03-06
Sara Kim | Provide security questionnaire answers (SOC2 scope, KMS use) | 2026-03-06
Maya Thompson | Send pricing for Dedicated vs Private + pilot SOW | 2026-03-03
Carlos Rivera | Prep list of required OS, driver and container image hashes for offline transfer | 2026-03-04
summary: Initial discovery for Verdant Labs' need for an on-prem, air-gapped Redwood Private deployment. Main concerns: offline updates, hardware compatibility (mixed NVIDIA A100 / A40 fleet), network isolation, KMS/HSM integration, and validation process for models. Agreement to run a pilot with 2-node cluster for benchmarking and to exchange hardware/network details; Redwood to provide offline install checklist and SOW options.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. We also have Carlos, our SE, and Liam from solutions. How are you all?
[00:10] Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Priya, Head of ML at Verdant. We have Alan and Sara here. Appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:16] Alan: yeah hi, quick note on timing, we only have 45 minutes so hop to it.
[00:22] Maya: Perfect. The goal today is to understand your constraints for an on-prem air-gapped deployment, compliance needs, and what success looks like. Carlos will cover technical bits.
[00:33] Carlos: Quick agenda: infra, network, security, update process, and pilot/benchmarks. Sound good?
[00:40] Priya: Sounds good. High level — we run models for clinical summarization and de-iden, can't send PHI to hosted services. So hosted Redwood is out for those workloads; we're evaluating Dedicated vs Private on-prem, but security team is leaning air-gapped Private.
[00:58] Sara: For compliance we need downloadable audit logs, integration with our HSM for key unwrapping, SAML SSO, RBAC mapping to groups, and SOC2 evidence for the install.
[01:12] Maya: Understood. We do support KMS/HSM integrations and the Private offering has audit log export and RBAC integration. For air-gapped installs we provide an offline bundle and documented install steps. Carlos, can you talk about that?
[01:26] Carlos: Sure. For air-gapped Private we produce signed container images and an offline installer tarball. Customer transfers via USB or internal registry. We also provide checksums and a verification script. There are a few pre-reqs: supported OS images (we publish exact distros), driver ranges (CUDA versions), and kernel modules.
[01:41] Tom: when you say signed images, are there image digests we can verify with our offline HSM? we need to ensure chain of custody.
[01:49] Carlos: Yes, we provide SHA256 digests and signed manifests. In many installs customers use their HSM to sign internal transfers; Redwood can coordinate the verification steps.
[01:58] Alan: Our fleet is mixed — three A100s, two A40s, some older T4s in edge clusters. NVLink is present on the A100 nodes, and we have an InfiniBand fabric. We cannot upgrade kernel on production without approval but can for a pilot.
[02:14] Carlos: That's useful to know. A100 with NVLink + IB is great for throughput. We usually recommend homogenous nodes for initial pilots, but we can run mixed. Kernel/driver combos: what CUDA and driver versions are you on?
[02:27] Alan: Right now CUDA 11.6 on the A100s, drivers 470.x on the older nodes, planning to move to 510 for some nodes.
[02:35] Carlos: Ok we have known compatibility windows — we'll send a compatibility matrix. For 11.6 we have a supported path but some performance optimizations require 510+. We'll note that in the compatibility pre-check.
[02:48] Priya: Another big question: how do offline model updates work? Our security team wants signed model artifacts and a repeatable validation pipeline inside the air-gapped network.
[02:59] Carlos: We support model versioning; customers can push models through the offline bundle or host them on an internal registry. Models are referenced by digest and can be signed. For validation, Redwood's console components can run locally and we ship evaluation harnesses as part of the bundle.
[03:13] Sara: Does the console phone-home for telemetry? We can't allow outbound connections.
[03:18] Liam: Good question. For air-gapped installs we have two modes: fully isolated with no telemetry and an 'allowlist' mode where specific telemetry endpoints are permitted. All telemetry can be buffered, and logs are exportable.
[03:30] Sara: We will need fully isolated; only manual exports.
[03:34] Maya: That's fine — we have customers with zero egress. The tradeoff is you lose automatic updates and our remote diagnostics, so we provide a runbook for manual triage.
[03:44] Tom: How do you handle secrets? We use an on-prem HSM (Entrust) and Vault for secrets.
[03:50] Carlos: Redwood Private can integrate with on-prem KMS/Vault for model keys and TLS certs. For HSM we support PKCS#11 flows to unwrap keys during bootstrapping. There is some engineering work to validate the provider — we'll capture that as a checklist item.
[04:05] Alan: Network topology: nodes are on a private VLAN, management jump boxes have controlled egress. For air-gapped we want the image transfer to go via the management jump box.
[04:15] Carlos: That's typical. We'll provide guidance for proxying the offline bundle and for internal registry setup.
[04:22] Priya: Performance expectations — for our summarization models we need p50 latency under 120ms for 1k token average requests at 50 QPS. Does Redwood support micro-batching / KV cache?
[04:35] Carlos: Yes, the runtime has KV cache support and continuous batching. Those features improve tail latency and throughput. On A100 NVLink clusters with a 2-node partition you can get good QoS, but we'll want to run a benchmark.
[04:48] Priya: So the pilot should include latency and throughput bench for our prompt sets.
[04:52] Maya: Agreed. Pilot scope typically is a small cluster (2-4 GPUs) with your representative prompts and a few models. We can do both perf and accuracy/regression checks.
[05:03] Alan: About licensing and pricing — is Private a flat license or usage?
[05:09] Maya: Private is usually a platform license + support; Dedicated is reserved capacity with usage components. We'll share options — pilot SOW is separate.
[05:17] Sara: For SOC2 and audit evidence, we'll need system logs for at least 1 year, and retention policy docs. Can you support encrypted-at-rest logs?
[05:27] Carlos: Yes, logs can be stored encrypted, and we can ship configurations to push logs into your on-prem ELK or Splunk. For audit we export FIM, access logs, and API audit trails.
[05:39] Priya: Any known blockers for completely air-gapped deployments?
[05:44] Carlos: Biggest practical blockers are kernel/driver mismatches and GPU firmware that requires cloud access for updates; we typically ask customers to confirm firmware levels and plan for out-of-band firmware upgrades. Some vendor firmware tools need internet access — often managed via vendor-supported jumpbox procedures.
[06:03] Alan: So if we have older T4 nodes with older firmware, we should flag them and exclude from the pilot.
[06:08] Maya: Yup that matches our recommendation.
[06:11] Tom: On the operational side, patching — how frequently do you ship security patches for the runtime, and how are CVEs communicated for an air-gapped site?
[06:21] Carlos: We publish security advisories; for air-gapped installs we provide an advisory bundle with CVE notes and mitigations. Patches are provided as offline packages with checksums. We'll work with your security team on a cadence.
[06:33] Priya: For model privacy, do you store any model logs externally?
[06:38] Liam: No, in fully isolated mode nothing leaves the network unless you export. If you choose allowlist mode we can stream minimal telemetry, but given PHI you should stay isolated.
[06:47] Sara: Can you integrate with our SSO provider (Okta) for user mapping?
[06:52] Carlos: Yes, we support SAML/OIDC, group mapping, and can map those to RBAC roles in the platform. For air-gapped installs the SSO flow is usually proxied through your internal IdP; we'll document the steps.
[07:04] Priya: Another item: model vetting — we need a sign-off workflow where a model is promoted from dev to prod after automated tests. Is that in the product?
[07:13] Maya: Redwood has a rollout feature and evaluation hooks. In Private, these run locally and you can gate promotion on eval results.
[07:20] Alan: On hardware — for the pilot we can provision two A100 nodes with 40GB and NVLink; they will be isolated. We'll send exact SKUs.
[07:29] Carlos: Great, that will give us a good perf baseline.
[07:33] Priya: Timeline — security wants proof-of-concept done within 3 weeks for leadership to approve budget. Is that realistic?
[07:41] Maya: If we get hardware inventory and a signed SOW this week we can target a pilot within two to three weeks. The critical path is image verification and HSM integration.
[07:51] Sara: On legal, we need a copy of your standard Private SOW and data processing addendum.
[07:57] Maya: Will send those. We have templates for on-prem installs and DPA.
[08:02] Tom: For troubleshooting, do you offer remote assist if we're fully isolated?
[08:07] Carlos: We offer a remote assist option that requires an outbound connection during the session, but many customers prefer to have an on-prem engineer run the diagnostic scripts and share results. We can remotely review logs you export via a secure file transfer, or do a limited, time-boxed remote session with your approval.
[08:26] Priya: What's the rollback story if we upgrade the runtime or models and see regressions?
[08:31] Carlos: We support version pinning and fast rollback to previous runtime or model. For model rollouts you can do canary or A/B and automatic fallback rules. In air-gapped mode all of those features are local.
[08:44] Maya: any other concerns we haven't touched?
[08:47] Alan: Licensing for GPUs — do you require a minimum cluster size?
[08:51] Maya: No strict minimum; pilot can be small. Production licensing depends on size and support tier. We'll include pricing bands.
[08:58] Priya: Ok — security wants a dry run of the install on staging before prod.
[09:03] Carlos: We recommend staging that mirrors prod network isolation; we can provide scripts to validate the environment.
[09:10] Sara: Can you provide references for previous air-gapped installs in regulated health customers?
[09:15] Maya: Yes — we'll share anonymized references and a short case study.
[09:20] Tom: Anything about telemetry schema? our privacy team will want exact fields.
[09:24] Liam: We'll share the telemetry schema; in isolated installs it's optional, but we can provide it for your security review.
[09:32] Priya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:35] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send on-prem install guide, air-gap checklist, pilot SOW and pricing, compatibility matrix, telemetry schema, and references. Verdant to send hardware inventory, network diagram, answers to the security questionnaire, and proposed pilot dates. SE sync to validate driver/CUDA compatibility.
[09:56] Alan: That matches. We'll target 2026-03-09 for pilot kickoff if all goes well.
[10:01] Sara: we'll aim to deliver inventory and questionnaire by 2026-03-06.
[10:06] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with meeting notes and the package. Thanks everyone.
[10:12] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:15] [END]
